rows: Evaluate toughened epoxy, hot/wet `Tg`, damage tolerance, prepreg process, certification, and allowables.
Resin choice is inseparable from certified process and environment.
Compare low-viscosity epoxy, vinyl ester, infusion distance, pot life, exotherm, and cost.
A great cured resin can fail manufacturing if viscosity/window are wrong.
Check vinyl ester vs UPE, hydrolysis resistance, osmotic blistering, glass compatibility, and repair.
Below-waterline exposure makes water resistance a primary design requirement.
Compare phenolic, BMI, smoke/toxicity, flame spread, processability, and mechanical tradeoffs.
Fire performance often trades against toughness and processing ease.
Use BMI, cyanate ester, thermoplastic options, dry/wet `Tg`, oxidation, and thermal cycling.
Quote dry and wet `Tg`; moisture plasticization changes design margin.
Consider PEEK/PPS thermoplastics, melt processing, welding, impact toughness, and temperature.
Thermoplastics improve recyclability but raise processing temperature and equipment demands.
Compare GF/PP stamping, CF/epoxy RTM, cycle time, tooling, cost, and crash requirements.
Mass production rewards cycle time as much as material performance.
Use E-glass/UPE or vinyl ester, durability, UV/water exposure, inspection, and installation labor.
Cheapest resin is not cheapest lifecycle choice if durability fails.
